data.title: CCI approves Advent International-backed firm's stake acquisition in Yatharth Hospitals
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- The Competition Commission of India (CCI) on Saturday approved the acquisition of a certain shareholding in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited by Rasmalai Limited, an entity indirectly controlled by funds managed or advised by global private equity firm Advent International.

In an official release, the competition regulator said, "The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of a certain shareholding of Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd. by Rasmalai Limited."

The proposed transaction involves Rasmalai Limited acquiring a stake in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited.

According to the CCI, Rasmalai Limited is incorporated in Cyprus and is primarily engaged in holding investments. The company currently has no business operations or presence in India.

The regulator said, "The Acquirer is indirectly controlled by investment funds managed and/or advised by Advent International, L.P. and/or its affiliates."

Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited operates a network of super-speciality hospitals in India, offering healthcare services, diagnostic facilities and advanced medical procedures across multiple medical specialities.

The approval clears the proposed transaction from the competition regulator's perspective.

The CCI release did not disclose the percentage of shareholding proposed to be acquired or the financial value of the transaction.

data.title: Fed's Collins says gradual rate hikes best to manage economic risks
data.description:
By Michael S. Derby

Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said on Saturday she supports a steady pace of modest interest rate increases because that path of action better manages economic uncertainties.

The risks on the real side of the economy were "two-sided", she said, which has implications for both the Fed’s job and inflation mandates and argues against taking aggressive action to target high levels of inflation.

In such an environment, "my current view is that a kind of steady, gradual approach for monetary policy is appropriate" Collins told reporters at a conference at her bank.

data.title: Uber Notifies Drivers After Unauthorized Access To Data Through Third-Party Provider
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Uber Technologies has informed affected drivers of a security incident involving a third-party service provider that resulted in unauthorized access to certain personal information.

According to a notice issued by the company on November 10, 2026, the service provider notified Uber on October 9 that an unauthorized party had compromised the provider's internal credentials and used them to access Uber's account.

Upon learning of the incident, Uber said it immediately disconnected its data links with the provider and began an investigation into the matter.

The investigation determined on October 13 that the compromised credentials had been used to access Uber-related data maintained by the service provider. Uber said the affected individuals are being notified because their personal information was among the data accessed.

The company said it continues to review the incident and contact impacted individuals.

data.title: 'Are you going to sell fabric cut-pieces?' How Noel Tata defied doubters to build a retail powerhouse
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- "Aap log cut-piece bechnewale hai kya?"

That was the incredulous query from an investor when the Tata Group went into apparel retail 27 years ago, in a country where modern retail was not a concept yet.

On Saturday, Noel Tata, who built and scaled Westside, Zudio and Star Bazaar under the Trent umbrella, recalled the scepticism of the time, when India's consumption engine was yet to turn on, and private labels were unheard of. In the decades that followed, Trent went on to beat at all expectations, the Tata Trusts chairman said at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi.

"When we first started our first shop, there were only two other shops of significance in India. It was a concept; modern retail was not understood," said Noel, who led Trent as managing director since 1999 and as chairman since 2014. He stepped down last month when he turned 70, in compliance with the Tata Group's retirement policy for non-executive directors.

From betting on private labels at the dawn of modern retail to building Zudio into a 1,000-store chain, Noel Tata's retail strategy centred on product ownership, affordable fashion and India's expanding consumption market.

The retail business has become one of the biggest consumer-facing ventures of Tata Group, with Trent Ltd operating more than 320 Westside stores and over 1,000 Zudio outlets. Zudio alone is on track to generate around Rs.15,000 crore in sales this year, selling nearly 400 million units, Tata said at the Summit.

Noel recalling the journey of building Trent comes at a time when the Tata Trusts he leads have questioned mounting losses at some of Tata Sons' newer businesses such as aviation and e-commerce.

In June 1999, the company formerly known as Lakme Ltd changed its name to Trent and appointed 42-year-old Noel N. Tata to its helm, with a monthly salary that topped out at Rs.1 lakh. At that time, its retail business included four Westside stores in Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Mumbai, covering about 80,000 sq ft of shop space.

Twenty-seven years later, Trent's FY2025-26 annual report tells a very different story. Total revenue from operations rose 17.2% to Rs.20,074 crore, and net profit for shareholders rose 11.2% to Rs.1,719.65 crore.

Trent now runs 1,286 stores across 321 cities, with more than 17.7 million sq ft of retail space. That is over 200 times its 1999 footprint. It added 289 stores in the year alone.

The change started with a sale. Lakme's brand names were sold to Hindustan Lever for Rs.110.03 crore, and the company took over its retail subsidiary, Trent (formerly Littlewoods International India), which Noel had managed.

In his latest letter to shareholders, Noel wrote that he remembers opening the first Westside on Bengaluru's Commercial Street in 1998, when modern fashion retail in India was "almost non-existent."

Trent's market cap totalled Rs.1,68,501 crore at the end of Friday, making it the fourth most valuable Tata Group company, behind Tata Consultancy Services Ltd, Tata Steel and Titan Co. Ltd.

The real growth came later. Zudio, the budget brand launched in 2016, had failed as a large store by 2020, before Trent redesigned it. In the next decade, it expanded to 963 stores in 313 cities, including six in the UAE. Westside has 300 stores. Revenue has grown by about 50% a year since FY22, when it was Rs.3,881 crore.

The journey, Tata said, was built on a decision that went against the conventional retail playbook: developing and selling the company's own brands instead of stocking established labels.

"One of the most significant decisions that we took when we first started, which was with Westside, was whether we became a branded retailer or whether we did our own private label brands. And we took the more difficult decision. We said we will do private label," he said.

The choice meant Trent had to take responsibility for designing products, sourcing fabric and managing the entire chain until the merchandise reached customers. Tata described the model as an early direct-to-consumer business in India, giving the retailer control over the product rather than simply acting as a distribution platform for other brands.

The business took time to find its footing. In its initial years, the team believed the Westside format could support about 10 stores across the country. A decade later, expectations had expanded to 50-60 stores, largely across metropolitan markets.

"They worked hard at it for 10 years, with lots of trial and error and patience, and finally, they hit the right note," Saurabh Mukherjea of Marcellus Investment Managers, whose funds own Trent shares, told Mint earlier.

Noel has avoided the acquisition track taken by rivals like Reliance Retail and Aditya Birla Fashion, focusing instead on Trent's own brands. Star, the grocery division, now makes 73% of its revenue from its own labels and runs 84 stores in 12 cities.

How big can Trent get? "Trent has the opportunity to be 10X its size, but don't ask me by when," Noel told Mint in 2024.

Trent's format was designed to offer aspirational products at affordable prices, with stores starting at around 6,000 sq ft and prices ranging from Rs.199 to Rs.999. A decade later, those price points remain unchanged, Tata said.

Zudio also broke away from conventional retail marketing. The chain has neither an e-commerce platform nor a website and has largely stayed away from advertising, relying instead on its physical store network and product quality.

"We've never been on e-commerce and, you know, never done any e-commerce at all," Tata said, adding that the company had not undertaken any advertising apart from a campaign marking the opening of its 1,000th store.

Tata attributed the expansion partly to the growing reach of consumption in India, particularly in smaller cities. Demand for better products was no longer restricted to metros, with tier-II and tier-III towns increasingly contributing to the consumption story. He also credited the broader expansion of India's economy for the opportunity, saying the growth in consumption was visible across socio-economic categories and geographies.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: All 10 reporting firms beat EPS estimates across seven sectors; 8 grow Y/Y profits
data.description:
Earnings season continues with 10 companies reporting quarterly results across utilities, industrials, financials, energy, communication services, materials, and information technology.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Out of the 10 companies reporting, all 10 exceeded EPS expectations. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth (while 1 declined and 1 had no prior-year comparison).

Top Line: Out of the 10 companies reporting, 8 exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Constellation Energy : advanced just over 10% post-earnings after reporting Q3 adjusted operating earnings of $5.06 per share, beating the $3.88 consensus estimate, alongside revenue of $9.55B (+45.4% Y/Y). Management raised and narrowed its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance to $12.50–$12.80 per share, citing Calpine accretion, strong commercial performance, and higher PJM capacity prices.

Ferguson Enterprises : climbed 11.22% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $9.03B (+9.5% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $310M, while non-GAAP EPS of $3.43 topped forecasts by $0.14. Growth was driven by 7.0% organic expansion and 2.7% from acquisitions, prompting management to raise its calendar 2026 net sales outlook to ~7% growth and narrow its adjusted operating margin target to 9.6%–9.8%.

KKR & Co. : climbed 2.0% post-earnings after delivering Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.78, surpassing the $1.58 consensus estimate, while revenue reached $2.61B (+8.8% Y/Y). Results were bolstered by record fee-related earnings of $1.32B and strong returns in infrastructure (+4%) and alternative credit (+3%), with the firm expecting to return over $40B to clients in 2026.

NRG Energy : gained just over 10% alongside a broader utility rally after reporting Q3 revenue of $9.47B (+24.0% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $180M, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.68, topping forecasts by $1.65. Management reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.90–$9.90 and projected 2027 adjusted EPS of $8.05–$10.05 ($9.05 midpoint).

Occidental Petroleum : rose 2.04% post-earnings after reporting better-than-expected Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.91 (beating by $0.44), even as revenue of $6.56B missed consensus estimates. A 32.5% Y/Y jump in average realized oil prices to $85.91/bbl helped offset a 2.5% dip in global production to 1.43M boe/day caused by maintenance and Gulf of Mexico curtailments, with Q4 output guided to 1.43M–1.47M boe/day, with output from the Permian Basin expected to ‌come in at 820K-840K boe/day.

Take-Two Interactive Software : rose 8.31% post-earnings in reaction to its FQ2 results and GTA 6 update, despite total net bookings falling 18% Y/Y to $1.60B (missing the $1.66B estimate) and EPS coming in at $1.00. Looking ahead, the company guided FY27 revenue to $8.0B–$8.2B and EPS to $0.57–$0.75, trailing consensus estimates.

TransDigm Group : rose 0.55% post-earnings as a soft profit outlook overshadowed a Q4 beat, with revenue rising 22.6% Y/Y to $2.99B (beating by ~$40M) and adjusted EPS of $12.44 topping the $12.21 consensus. While management projected FY27 revenue of $11.95B–$12.15B above estimates, its FY27 adjusted EPS forecast of $47.09–$47.94 fell short of the $48.66 consensus amid higher borrowing costs.

Vylor Inc. : fell 0.06% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $938M (-0.6% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $19.94M, while non-GAAP EPS of -$0.42 topped expectations by $0.10. Supported by continued technology adoption, the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 outlook for adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of ~$2.8B and EPS of $2.25–$2.35 vs. consensus of $2.38.

Applied Materials : rose 1.4% in extended trading after reporting Q4 FY2026 revenue of $10.41B (+53% Y/Y), surpassing the $10.3B estimate, while adjusted EPS of $4.16 beat the $4.05 consensus. Fueled by strong AI-driven semiconductor demand, the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $10.6B–$11.6B ($11.1B midpoint) and adjusted EPS to $4.15–$4.55 ($4.35 midpoint), both above Street forecasts.

Cisco Systems : perked up 2% in early post-market trading after Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 24% Y/Y to $18.5B (beating the $18.13B estimate) and adjusted EPS of $1.40 topped the $1.33 consensus. Performance was propelled by 43% Y/Y growth in networking ($11.13B), prompting Cisco to raise its FY2027 adjusted EPS outlook to $5.47–$5.52 and revenue guidance to $74.8B–$75.8B, with AI hyperscaler revenue expected to reach $9B.

Earnings next week:

As earnings season rolls on, investors are tracking key reports across communication services, consumer discretionary, consumer staples, and information technology.

Key reports to watch include The Walt Disney Company , The Home Depot , Lowe's Companies , Ross Stores , The TJX Companies , Target Corporation , Tyson Foods , Walmart , NVIDIA Corporation , Palo Alto Networks , Intuit , Keysight Technologies , and Everpure .

data.title: Hungary recovers $20 million cash in probe of Orban minister
data.description:
By Gergely Szakacs

Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, some buried in forests or hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, in a bribery investigation into Miklos Sesztak, a minister under former leader Viktor Orban.

Prime Minister Peter Magyar ousted Orban after 16 years in power in an April election, pledging to mend ties with the European Union strained by years of disagreements under Orban, and to launch a sweeping investigation into allegations of graft.

The clampdown is part of an anti-graft drive the centre-right Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory", which 70% of respondents rated as "very important" in a survey by the pollster Median carried by news website HVG this week.

"During searches, investigators found large amounts of cash buried in forests, hidden in farm buildings, warehouses and a residential property, and stored in a high-value safe in a secluded location," the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said late on Friday.

Finance Minister Andras Karman said it took a dozen State Treasury workers eight hours using banknote counters to count the cash that had been retrieved.

Magyar said the recovered cash signalled the end of what he described as a "mafia" led by Orban's right-wing Fidesz party and his Christian Democrat allies during Orban's 16-year rule.

Fidesz wrote in a Facebook post that it hoped Sesztak was not connected to the cash.

"Since the change of regime, every lawmaker in Hungary has sworn an oath to abide by and enforce the law. Fidesz-KDNP (Christian Democrats) cannot associate itself with anyone who fails to do so. We trust that the images published by the NVVH (asset recovery office) have nothing to do with Miklos Sesztak," Fidesz wrote.

Sesztak — Orban's development minister from 2014 to 2018 — has denied wrongdoing. His lawyer, Gabor Papp, did not respond to a request for comment on the recovery office's statement. But he told local news website Telex the seized cash did not belong to Sesztak, a member of parliament's Economic and Energy Affairs Committee. He added that the bribery case also involved other suspects.

FORMER MINISTER FACING CALL TO RELINQUISH HIS MANDATE

But Bence Retvari, parliamentary group leader of the Christian Democrats, said Sesztak, the party's vice chair, should relinquish his parliamentary mandate as he seeks to clear his name.

"This is an individual criminal case, and the criminal proceedings must be kept strictly separate from our political community," Retvari said on Facebook.

"Peter Magyar wants to use it to portray the entire right as a criminal organisation. We reject this in the strongest possible terms!"

In separate investigations, two former ministers from Orban's government and former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsy are under arrest over graft accusations. They have denied wrongdoing.

Authorities have also detained Orban's brother in a people-smuggling case that the former leader has dismissed as an act of political revenge.

Gabor Torok, a political scientist, said the images of the cash were so vivid they likely spelled doom for Fidesz, whose support fell by half from its pre-election level to 16% of voters in November, a Median survey showed.

($1 = 330.82 forints, 0.9074 euros)

data.title: Who is Rene Haas? Arm CEO emerges as potential Nvidia chief after Jensen Huang's exit; what makes him a frontrunner?
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Nvidia has reportedly approached Arm Holdings chief executive Rene Haas as it explores potential successors to Jensen Huang, according to a Financial Times report.

Haas, who spent seven years at Nvidia before joining Arm in 2013, is among several names being reportedly considered for the top job at the US chipmaker.

However, there is no certainty that Haas will be offered the position or agree to take it up.

Nvidia's board has said it is still in the process of selecting an executive search firm and has not formally approached any potential candidates.

The reported development comes amid speculation over Nvidia's leadership transition, with some employees reportedly urging the board to reconsider its decision and bring back Huang.

Rene Anthony Andrada Haas, 64, is an American technology executive who has led Arm Holdings since February 2022.

He is also a member of the British chipmaker's board and a director of its parent company, Japan's SoftBank Group.

Haas has more than three decades of experience in the semiconductor and computing industries.

Before taking charge of Arm, he spent seven years at Nvidia, where he rose to become vice president and general manager of its computing products business.

He joined Arm in 2013 and went on to hold several senior leadership positions before being appointed its chief executive in 2022.

His familiarity with Nvidia's operations, engineering culture and business strategy, combined with his experience running a publicly listed semiconductor company, has made him a potential contender for the role.

Under Haas, Arm has expanded its focus beyond its traditional strength in mobile phone processors to areas such as artificial intelligence, data centres, automotive computing and high-performance processors.

One of his major milestones was overseeing Arm's return to public markets through its Nasdaq initial public offering (IPO) in September 2023. The listing was among the biggest stock market debuts of that year.

Arm does not typically manufacture chips itself. Instead, it develops processor architectures and intellectual property that other companies license to design semiconductors for smartphones, computers, data centres and connected devices.

Its technology is used across a broad range of computing products, giving Haas experience in an industry that is increasingly central to the global AI boom.

Nvidia's board is searching for a permanent successor after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and chief executive on November 12.

The company appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO while it considers internal and external candidates.

The leadership crisis followed reports about Huang's extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of being a spy.

The espionage allegation has not been independently established, and Beijing has denied it.

The board has said it is selecting an executive search firm and has not formally engaged any potential candidates. This is an important distinction from the Financial Times report that it approached Haas.

While the board considers potential successors, a section of Nvidia's workforce has reportedly called for Huang to return.

According to a report by technology publication Wired, an internal post by a longtime Nvidia engineer urging the board to take employee sentiment into account has attracted more than 1,600 comments. Several employees reportedly called for Huang's reinstatement.

Billionaire Elon Musk also said on X that a petition was being organised to bring Huang back and that he would sign it. It remains unclear whether Musk was referring to the internal employee campaign.

Whoever takes over from Huang will inherit a company at the centre of the global artificial intelligence boom, but also one facing mounting geopolitical, regulatory and competitive pressures.

Huang led Nvidia for more than three decades, overseeing its transformation from a graphics-processing company into a dominant supplier of AI chips.

His role extended beyond product development to strategic investments, relationships with technology companies and negotiations surrounding semiconductor exports to China.

The next chief executive will have to navigate growing scrutiny from US lawmakers over advanced chip exports to China, intensifying competition in AI computing and the challenge of sustaining Nvidia's position in the global semiconductor market.

data.title: Jensen Huang Is Out. What Happens to Nvidia Stock Now?
data.description:
Editor’s Note: Jensen Huang’s sudden departure from Nvidia has left investors with some big questions. Is the AI chip giant still a buy? And what happens to the AI boom without one of its most influential leaders? My colleague Louis Navellier has some thoughts. But he also sees a much bigger shift taking place on Wall Street – one he explored during his recent Fed Warning 2027 presentation.

Today, Louis explains whether he’s still holding Nvidia, where Wall Street’s money is moving, and why yesterday’s market leaders may not be tomorrow’s winners. He’ll also talk more about his Fed Warning 2027 and how to prepare for what comes next.

What a difference a week makes, folks.

Just a few days ago, Jensen Huang was the face of the AI Revolution. As CEO of Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), he was one of the most powerful figures in technology, with investors hanging on his every word.

Today, he’s out of a job.

His shocking resignation has sent shock waves through Wall Street, raising serious questions about Nvidia’s future – and what comes next for the AI boom.

But here’s something you may find interesting.

This past Thursday, I shared my special Fed Warning 2027 presentation.

We talked about the market’s narrowing list of winners, the rotation taking place on Wall Street, and where I see the biggest opportunities emerging as we head into 2027.

I also unveiled something I’ve been working on for quite some time: my brand-new investment service, Prime Portfolio.

In fact, last weekend, I personally selected the first 25 stocks for my new portfolio.

And Nvidia wasn’t one of them.

Now, don’t misunderstand me. Even after Huang’s resignation, I still believe Nvidia’s has tremendous earnings power, and I’ll be watching its upcoming earnings report closely.

But the market is rotating, and yesterday’s winners won’t necessarily lead tomorrow.

That’s precisely why I built Prime Portfolio. It goes well beyond stock picks, with tools to help you allocate your money, monitor your holdings, and know when to make a change.

Today, I’ll explain what Huang’s departure means for Nvidia, why the market’s rotation is so important, and how my new service is designed to help you stay on the right side of it.

What Jensen Huang’s Resignation Means for Nvidia Stock

I’ll admit, I didn’t see Jensen Huang’s resignation coming.

On Monday, I expected the Nvidia Board of Directors and the U.S. government to eventually clear Huang of wrongdoing. As recently as Wednesday, I remained confident he would weather the storm.

Clearly, things changed in a hurry.

Reports of Huang’s relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence have been raising questions about whether sensitive information had been compromised for a few days. Then on Wednesday night, news of a second extramarital affair emerged. By Thursday morning, Huang had resigned, and longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

There are still plenty of unanswered questions:

  • Was sensitive information exposed? 
  • What happens to Nvidia’s relationship with China? 
  • And who can replace the visionary leader who built Nvidia into the dominant force in AI chips?

Should Investors Sell Nvidia Stock?

But here’s what I want you to remember. Nvidia’s earnings power didn’t disappear overnight.

Before all this drama, analysts were forecasting third-quarter sales growth of about 91% and earnings growth of 90%. Those are stunning numbers. And while the leadership shakeup creates uncertainty, Nvidia still has its technology, its customers, and enormous demand for the chips powering the AI Revolution.

The company is scheduled to report earnings on November 17. I’ll be paying especially close attention to management’s guidance and whether analysts begin cutting their estimates.

For now, I’m recommending that investors hang on to their Nvidia shares while we assess the situation.

The bottom line: I don’t make investment decisions based on shocking headlines alone. I follow the sales, earnings, and underlying strength of a business.

And right now, there’s another important development taking place on Wall Street that investors shouldn’t overlook.

Why Nvidia Isn’t the Only Stock Investors Should Be Watching

You see, folks, the market’s rotation didn’t begin with Jensen Huang’s resignation.

It’s been underway for some time.

Take IREN Ltd. (IREN), for example.

On November 5, the AI neocloud company reported strong top-line growth, with revenue jumping 66% to $228.3 million as AI cloud sales nearly tripled. However, it also posted a steep $263 million net loss – missing earnings estimates – while warning of rising costs and a delay to its $4 billion annual recurring revenue (ARR) target.

data.title: Saudi Water Authority cancels Va Tech Wabag’s 300 MLD desalination project in Yanbu
data.description:
Water technology company Va Tech Wabag said on Saturday that the Saudi Water Authority had cancelled an order for a 300 MLD mega seawater desalination plant earlier awarded to Wabag.

“Subsequent to the award, the company had completed the necessary formalities and executed the contract, which was submitted to the customer (Saudi Water Authority) for their counter-signature and formal commencement of the project. However, the customer has now notified all tender participants through the Etimad portal (Electronic Government Procurement and Tendering Platform of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia) that the said tender has been cancelled due to internal reasons attributable to the customer,” Va Tech Wabag said.

Wabag said it is in the process of approaching the customer to understand the reason in better detail and the next course of action.

The order is related to the design, engineering, supply, construction, and commissioning of a 300 MLD Mega Desalination plant at Yanbu, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

data.title: Patanjali Foods Q2 revenue rises 15.55% to Rs 11,323 crore, edible oil business hits record high
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Patanjali Foods Limited reported a 15.55 per cent year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 11,322.58 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27, driven by strong growth in its edible oils business, which recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue.

According to the company's unaudited financial results released on Saturday, revenue from operations rose from Rs 9,798.84 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

The company said, "The Edible Oils segment recorded its highest-ever revenue of Rs. 8,532.25 crores, registering 22.39% YoY growth."

The edible oils segment reported earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of Rs 256.22 crore, with a margin of 3 per cent.

At the company level, operating EBITDA, excluding exceptional items, stood at Rs 425.63 crore, with a margin of 3.76 per cent. Profit before tax stood at Rs 409.02 crore, translating into a margin of 3.59 per cent.

Meanwhile, the company's fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) segment generated revenue of Rs 2,923.48 crore during the quarter, contributing 25.50 per cent to revenue from operations, excluding inter-segment revenue.

The FMCG segment reported EBITDA of Rs 221.33 crore, with a margin of 7.57 per cent. It contributed 45.04 per cent to the company's segment EBITDA, excluding unallocable income.

Within the FMCG business, the biscuits division recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 638.31 crore, registering a growth of 27.69 per cent year-on-year.

The company's home and personal care business also reported revenue growth of 11.06 per cent to Rs 713.88 crore, supported by a 25.58 per cent increase in skin care revenue.

Commenting on the quarterly performance, Sanjeev Asthana, Chief Executive Officer of Patanjali Foods Limited, said, "Q2FY27 performance reflected the resilience of our integrated business model across branded edible oils, upstream oil palm plantations and growing FMCG portfolio."

For the first half of FY27, Patanjali Foods reported its highest-ever revenue from operations of Rs 22,660.03 crore, registering a growth of 22.06 per cent compared to the corresponding period last year.

Operating EBITDA for the six-month period stood at Rs 969.03 crore, with a margin of 4.28 per cent.

Looking ahead, the company expects demand momentum to continue, supported by festive consumption and the upcoming wedding season.

"With the recent festive season and the upcoming wedding season, we expect growth momentum to continue," Asthana said.

The company said it would continue focusing on premiumisation, expanding its edible oils and FMCG portfolio, and strengthening its oil palm plantation business.

data.title: TVS Electronics Q2 Results: Company posts ₹1.41 crore net loss; revenue falls 9.4%
data.description:
TVS Electronics Ltd on Saturday, November 14, reported a net loss of ₹1.41 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, compared with a net profit of ₹1.5 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to the company’s regulatory filing.

Sequentially, however, the company narrowed its net loss from ₹6.62 crore reported in the June 2026 quarter.

Revenue from operations declined 9.4% year-on-year to ₹116.16 crore in Q2 FY27, down from ₹127.50 crore in the year-ago quarter. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, operational revenue increased 9.54% to ₹106.04 crore.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) fell 37% YoY to ₹3.36 crore, compared with ₹5.33 crore in Q2 FY26. EBITDA margin contracted to 2.90% during the quarter from 4.16% a year earlier.

Total expenses for the quarter stood at ₹118.48 crore, down 7.57% from ₹128.18 crore in the same period last year. Loss before tax came in at ₹1.89 crore, against a profit before tax of ₹1.15 crore in Q2 FY26.

Segment-wise, revenue from the Products & Solutions business declined 14.63% YoY to ₹79.39 crore from ₹92.99 crore, posting a segment loss before interest and tax of ₹1.74 crore compared with a profit of ₹4.27 crore a year ago. Meanwhile, revenue from Customer Support Services rose 6.52% YoY to ₹36.77 crore from ₹34.52 crore, returning to profitability with a segment profit of ₹1.01 crore against a loss of ₹3.24 crore in Q2 FY26.

Alongside the quarterly results, the Board of Directors approved the appointment of Narayan Keelveedhi Seshadri as an Additional Director in the category of Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director for a term of five consecutive years, effective November 14.

data.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute pitches mining as a fix for Scotland's wasted wind power
data.description:
Britain has a strange energy habit. It pays Scottish wind farms to switch off, then pays gas plants elsewhere to switch on.

A report from the Bitcoin Policy Institute (BPI) argues there is a better use for that surplus power: Bitcoin mining. The pitch is simple. If the electricity can't reach the people who need it, bring a buyer to the electricity instead.

The scale of the problem is not small. In 2024, Britain paid wind farms £393 million to curtail 8.3 TWh of output.

Scotland carries almost all of that burden. According to the research findings, 98% of the curtailed output came from Scotland.

The cause is geography plus wiring. Scottish wind capacity has grown faster than the transmission lines needed to carry power south to England, where demand is highest.

So grid operators end up running a two-sided bill. They compensate Scottish wind farms for staying idle while compensating gas-fired stations further south for ramping up.

The trend is moving in the wrong direction. The value of wind curtailment in Britain rose 91% year over year, per the research findings.

The report casts Bitcoin miners as buyers of last resort. They can soak up power that would otherwise go unused, and they don't need it delivered anywhere.

The key selling point is flexibility. Mining rigs can ramp consumption up or down quickly based on how much energy is available.

That sets them apart from what the report calls firm loads, such as AI data centers. Those facilities need steady, uninterrupted power, which makes them a poor match for a supply that comes and goes with the weather.

A separate modeling analysis from May 2026 put some figures on the idea. It found that a 20 MW mining operation sitting alongside a 100 MW wind farm could use 83% of the farm's curtailed energy.

The same analysis estimated this setup could lift overall system revenue by 32%. It also showed the wind farm's effective capacity factor rising from 29% to 32%.

The report doesn't stop at the energy argument. It also flags obstacles that could keep Britain from becoming a serious Bitcoin hub.

Banking restrictions top the list. The report also points to inconsistent investment and tax rules as a drag on competitiveness.

That tension is notable because Britain's legal footing is relatively strong. The research findings note that Bitcoin has legal recognition as property in the UK.

Bitcoin Policy UK has also published several papers and podcasts on the topic. Their focus has been on mining as a source of demand-side flexibility for the grid and as a tool to support renewable energy targets.

The mining-for-curtailment argument isn't new globally. What makes the Scottish case stand out is how concentrated the waste is, with nearly all of Britain's curtailment piling up in one region behind one set of transmission bottlenecks.

data.title: Italy fines Meta $887 million over Android users' data access
data.description:
Italy's data protection agency said on Saturday it had fined Meta Platforms €805 million ($887 million) after finding the company had accessed Android users' photographs and videos without obtaining their consent or informing them.

  • Meta had access to Android users' photos and videos through a Facebook app feature that suggested content from users' personal galleries that they could post, the authority said in a statement

  • Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately, it added

  • Meta was not immediately available for comment

  • The investigation, which began in 2025, did not cover the possible use of the content to train artificial intelligence models, a practice Meta denied, the authority said

  • It added that it reserved the right to assess separately a new feature, launched in 2026, that allows content from users' galleries to be processed in the cloud

  • The fine is equivalent to about 0.47% of the group's global revenue, the authority said

($1 = 0.9074 euros)

"This is likely ADBE's most important Firefly Foundry partnership and deal yet, and success could usher in additional interest from other media entities," Altmann wrote.

BTIG currently forecasts that Adobe's full-year fiscal 2026 revenue will increase by 12% year over year and by 10% in fiscal year 2027. It projects free cash flow margins of 40% and 41%, respectively.

data.title: BoE's Greene says acting proactively now on inflation would 'screw' things up the least
data.description:
Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said on Saturday it was better to act proactively now to get on top of inflation than to take a more cautious approach and risk significant second-round effects.

Greene was among the majority of Monetary Policy Committee members who at the BoE's November meeting voted to raise borrowing costs to 4% from 3.75%, and had previously been part of a minority calling for an earlier rate hike.

"When you have no idea where inflation is going, when you're facing uncertainty, I think you need to adopt an attitude of how can I screw this up the least?" she told a conference held by the Centre for European Reform.

Greene restated her view that, given the uncertainty about the inflation outlook, it was less risky for the BoE to raise rates too much and then have to cut them if second-round effects did not materialise, than to wait too long to tighten policy and thereby risk letting inflation get out of hand.

"I think the risk of not getting on top of inflation coming out of a period when we've had inflation over target for the best part of about five-and-a-half years, that's the bigger risk, that would be the bigger policy mistake," she said.

"So I think there's a benefit in acting proactively in terms of kind of screwing it up the least."

Greene wrote earlier this week that it was appropriate for the BoE to "proactively tighten" its monetary policy stance to guard against the risk of pay growth getting stuck at around 3.5% or higher and firms passing the costs on through higher inflation.

Financial markets are betting on the BoE hiking interest rates again in December and following that up with two or possibly three more quarter-point moves in 2027.

BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill told the Financial Times in an interview published on Saturday it was likely there would be a need to raise rates further in 2027, over and above an increase at the next meeting in December.

data.title: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw believes the Microsoft outage creates opportunity for homegrown suite Zoho - here's how
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw believes the recent global Microsoft outage creates an opportunity for Sridhar Vembu-led Zoho to offer its services as a viable alternative. In a post on social media and subsequent responses to users, she said the homegrown brand is well-positioned to make a move.

Mazumdar-Shaw took to X (formerly known as Twitter), to react to the Microsoft outage. She termed it "an unexpected opportunity for Zoho to be an alternate backup MIS for India Inc given such unforeseen events". MIS is management information system.

Notably, Microsoft on Saturday said it has fully restored its flagship software and ended an outage that paralysed government offices, traders and businesses around the world, Bloomberg reported.

"All products are operational," according to a service health status update on its website. A "backlog of email messages has been processed, thus this issue is remediated," it said of its Microsoft 365 services.

Notably, the global Microsoft outage caused massive stops to business and critical infrastructure as its Windows operating system and productivity apps remain the top choice for many. There has been renewed criticism over the risk of a single provider holding so much power.

To be sure, the Microsoft outage on Friday was felt around the world, with people in over 70 countries, including India, impacted, as per data on Downdetector. The company's M365 software bundle has over 450 million commercial users, as per the Bloomberg report.

When asked, why Zoho, by a user, the Mazumdar-Shaw acknowledged that it was the only homegrown system she is aware of. Another user questioned why there is a need for global outages to create opportunity for Indian companies to "build our own", Mazumdar-Shaw stated: "It's always about events that create opportunities".

Responding to the executive's posts, some users noted that Zoho may not have the required capacity to handle loads that Microsoft does, some others noted that there are free alternatives, and other felt that in the large scheme of things they would continue with Microsoft products.

William Blair & Co. analyst Jason Ader wrote in a note, "We do not expect the incident to meaningfully change Microsoft's competitive position in the near term, given the high cost and complexity of replacing deeply embedded productivity workflows. Longer term, however, it could make some customers more receptive to alternatives, particularly Google Workspace and emerging productivity offerings from Anthropic unveiled earlier this week."

Notably, in India, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) said in a written reply to Lok Sabha last December said that the Centre migrated nearly 12.68 lakh official email accounts from various ministries and departments to a Zoho-based platform. Of these, 7.45 lakh accounts were of central government employees, it added.

The migration was carried out through the National Informatics Centre (NIC), which remains the mandated provider of official email services for government ministries and departments, Jitin Prasada, Minister of State, MeitY said in the response.

Zoho Mail is a secure email service launched by the multinational technology firm Zoho Corporation, a Chennai-based software services company which was co-founded by Vembu and Tony Tomas in 1996.
